claims.claim: Scrap power banks for sale in Ibadan.

risks.risk: Whether the power banks are actually dead/non-working vs. just cosmetically damaged (this heavily affects value).
risks.proof: A short video showing each unit charging a phone (or showing no output) plus any LED indicators when powered/plugged in.

risks.risk: Capacity (mAh) and cell quality are unknown; scrap units can vary widely in value.
risks.proof: Clear photo of the label/sticker showing capacity (mAh), voltage, and input/output specs (or open/inside photo if allowed).
risks.if_unproven: Priced at the lowest end for scrap power banks due to unknown capacity.

risks.risk: Missing accessories/ports damage (some may be missing cables, have broken USB ports, or damaged connectors).
risks.proof: Close-up photos of both ends/ports (USB output/input) and what exactly is included in the package.

risks.risk: Safety risk: swollen/leaking/bad cells (fire risk) is not visible here.
risks.proof: Photos showing the full body for swelling, dents, leakage, and a close-up of any venting/bulging areas.
risks.if_unproven: Priced as unsafe/for parts only (no premium).

proof_requests: Show a clear close-up of each power bank’s label/sticker (capacity mAh and input/output specs).
Show ports clearly (USB input/output) for both units.
Video test: plug in and show LED/charging behavior; then test output by charging a phone (or demonstrate no output).
response.reason: From the photo, these appear to be power-bank style items, but there’s no readable capacity/brand and no proof they are truly scrap/non-working; without that, a reliable worst-case price cannot be set.
